---
title: "JAXCMR"
description: "Specify memory-search models, generate recall predictions, and compare them with behavior."
---

## What the library does

JAXCMR is a Python library for computational models of memory search, including
Context Maintenance and Retrieval (CMR) models. It lets researchers specify study
events, generate recall predictions, analyse observed and simulated behavior,
and estimate model parameters. It uses JAX for numerical calculations.

A modeling project brings together a theoretical account, an experiment and a
way to compare predictions with observations. JAXCMR supplies tools for each of
these activities. The researcher chooses the model assumptions, the behavior to
explain and the comparisons that address the research question.

## How the activities connect

An experiment supplies sequences of presented items and recorded recall
responses. Behavioral analyses describe those responses: for example, how
recall varies with an item's position in the study list, or how people move
between items during recall. These summaries identify patterns a model might
need to explain.

A model processes study events using a set of parameters. It can assign
probabilities to possible responses and generate simulated recall sequences.
Applying the same behavioral analyses to simulated and observed responses makes
their patterns comparable.

Likelihood evaluates the observed response sequences under a model and its
parameters. Fitting searches for parameter values that improve a chosen
objective, such as likelihood or agreement between behavioral summaries. The
fitted parameters can then be used to generate and examine predictions. The
choice of fitting objective determines what agreement the fitting procedure
seeks.

## Where to start

**[Set up JAXCMR in VS Code](getting-started.qmd)** on an Apple Silicon Mac.
The setup page assumes no previous Python experience and ends with a working
notebook environment. It is prepared for the planned 0.2.0 release; installation
from PyPI still needs to be confirmed before the instructions are ready to use.

Continue with the **[Templates](templates.qmd)** for fourteen complete procedures
using data from the war-photo-recall experiment: behavioral analyses, fitting,
simulation, parameter exploration and model comparison. Each chapter includes its notebook and required inputs.

The **[repository](https://github.com/githubpsyche/jaxcmr)** contains the library,
tests and research material. Other templates remain research examples with
varying dependencies and maintenance status, outside this prepared set.
